source_meta._title: Debug messages aren't prefixed with gray color indicators

stor.environment: Minecraft: Java Edition 1.19.1 Pre-release 6 using an unmodified client. Use a fresh single-player world with commands enabled as the simplest deterministic environment; no dedicated server or additional player is required by the report. Use default chat and keyboard controls unless they have been rebound.
preconditions: Launch exactly Minecraft: Java Edition 1.19.1 Pre-release 6, not the listed fix version 1.19.1 Release Candidate 2 or a newer release.
Create or open a world in which the player has permission to execute commands. For a fresh single-player world, set Allow Cheats to ON during world creation.
Ensure chat is not hidden. If necessary, open Esc -> Options -> Chat Settings and set Chat to Shown.
Ensure command feedback is enabled. This is enabled by default in a fresh world; if it was previously disabled, execute /gamerule sendCommandFeedback true before starting the listed steps.
Use a keyboard capable of sending the F3+B debug-key combination. On keyboards where the function row controls media features, the Fn key may also need to be held.
The player must be fully loaded into the world, with normal movement and keyboard input responding.

steps.action: Start Minecraft using the installation for Java Edition 1.19.1 Pre-release 6, then open the command-enabled test world.
steps.success_cue: The player is present in the world and the pause or loading screen is no longer displayed.

steps.action: Wait for the world to finish its initial loading before sending any input.
steps.success_cue: Nearby terrain is rendered, the player can move normally, and keyboard input responds without a loading delay.

steps.action: Open the in-game chat input using the Open Chat control; its default key is T.
steps.success_cue: A chat input field is visible at the bottom of the screen and is ready to accept text.

steps.action: Enter the report's command exactly as written, including the leading slash, and press Enter to execute it as the current player.
steps.success_cue: The chat input closes and a command-feedback message concerning the addition of the test tag appears in the chat area. If an insufficient-permission or unknown-command error appears instead, stop and enable commands before retrying in a fresh world.

steps.action: Use the command-feedback message as the control system message. Inspect the left side of that message and confirm that its gray system-message color indicator is visible before proceeding.
steps.success_cue: The command-feedback line remains identifiable in chat and has a gray indicator immediately to its left, establishing the report's control condition.

steps.action: With the game world active and no menu or chat input field open, invoke the debug hitbox function once. Hold F3 and tap B; on keyboards that reserve function keys for media controls, hold Fn as well while sending F3+B. Do not invoke the combination a second time before observation.
steps.success_cue: A debug status message indicating that hitboxes were shown or hidden has just appeared in the chat area, confirming that the debug function executed.

stor.handoff_condition: The F3+B debug function has just executed once, and its resulting debug status message is visible in the chat area. Begin observation of that message and its left-side indicator presentation without pressing F3+B again.
uncertainties: The report does not specify single-player versus multiplayer, game mode, world seed, operating system, or customized controls. A fresh command-enabled single-player world with default controls is selected as the minimal deterministic setup.
The report permits any debug function and gives F3+B as its example. This plan uses F3+B exactly to avoid introducing an unreported alternative.

The report does not explicitly state the command-feedback gamerule or chat visibility settings. Their enabled states are necessary for the two comparison messages to be visible and are normally present in a fresh world.
No external version verification was needed because the affected version, exact command, and debug-key combination are all supplied directly by the report.
